🚀 Exciting Opportunity for Game Developers! 🚀

Hello, developers!
I'm currently working on a new football game called I.F.C – Iconic Football Champions, and I'm looking for passionate game developers who want to collaborate in creating an epic football experience. The game will feature legendary players from past and future eras, and we plan to combine old-school gameplay with cutting-edge graphics and game modes.

What’s in it for you?

A chance to work on a game with a unique concept!

Competitive revenue sharing

Collaborate with a passionate team on something truly groundbreaking.

Flexible and creative input

Possibility to join in as a long-term partner


I need developers skilled in:

Game Design / Development

Football Simulation & AI Programming

3D Modelling / Animation

Graphics and User Interface Design


This is an amazing opportunity for those looking to make an impact on the gaming world and football culture. I'm offering a competitive share of the game profits (up to 40%) or an initial fee for your work.

If you're interested in being part of this journey and want to know more, DM me directly! I’m happy to discuss all the details.

Let’s make history together with I.F.C – Iconic Football Champions! ⚽🎮

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body:
I hope you manage to get your project made, but a few words of advice.

1. You need to get way more specific. Not just in this kind of post, but about your project in general. Get rid of the buzzwords. Before you go out looking for people, really workshop your project and scope. That *is* a task in and of itself. It doesn't all need to be final, but being able to say what you want to include and, more importantly, DON'T want to include, is crucial.

2. This sounds like a first (major) project. Don't assume you'll make money. Make this game because you want to make it, not because you see a payoff in the future. If it succeeds, cool, unexpected money, but don't bet the house on it. 

3. Be honest. Now, aside from questionable spelling in the title, throwing out promises of money feels really suspicious and fishy. If you're looking for a collaborator on this project, maybe go into more detail on the things that make it cool first and try and find someone equally excited. That would be more promising imho.

4. Unless you're Mr. EA or Dr. Ubisoft, you should probably steer clear of anything that requires licensing of likenesses or brands.
